newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Paccar launches bid for Dutch DAF Trucks.
newsitem.headline: Paccar launches bid for Dutch DAF Trucks.

text.p: U.S. truckmaker Paccar Inc. has made a 933 million guilder ($543.8 million) bid to take over the privately held Dutch company DAF Trucks NV, DAF said Monday.
DAF Trucks is the successor company to DAF NV, which was declared bankrupt in 1993. Its single biggest shareholder is the Dutch government, with a stake of just under 40 percent.
DAF Trucks said Bellevue, Wash.-based Paccar's offer had the support of DAF's two main management organs, the executive board and the supervisory board. The offer will close Nov. 15.
Paccar is the world's third-largest producer of heavy trucks, with a 1995 output of over 54,000 vehicles.
DAF Trucks made over 16,600 vehicles at its Eindhoven plant in 1995 and claims a 9 percent shares of the West European market for trucks heavier than 15 metric tons.
Paccar has four plants in the United States and has over 20 percent of the North American market for heavy trucks.
The company, which makes trucks under the Peterbilt, Kenworth and Foden brand names, also has production facilities in Britain, Australia and Mexico.
DAF Trucks quoted its chairman, Cor Baan, as saying that said Paccar planned to run DAF Trucks as an independent unit, retaining the DAF and Leyland DAF brand names.

Paccar had a net profit of $253 million on sales of $4.6 billion in 1995. DAF Trucks had profits of 164 million guilders ($95.6 million)) on sales of 2.9 billion guilders ($1.7 billion) in the same year.
DAF Trucks said the overall bid included 33 million guilders ($19.2 million) for a 25 percent stake in its Belgian unit held by Flemish regional institutions.
